This script integrates lipidomic and metabolomic data from the E5 timeseries project to:

1. Test effects of species and timepoint on the combined lipid + metabolite profile
2. Identify lipids and metabolites that drive separation between species and across time
3. Identify coordinated (correlated and lag-correlated) changes between the two datasets

# Set Up

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

Load libraries.

```{r}
library(mixOmics)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(readxl)
library(vegan)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(patchwork)
```

Set consistent color palettes.

```{r}
species_cols  <- c("Acropora" = "#1b7837", "Pocillopora" = "#762a83", "Porites" = "#d95f02")
timepoint_cols <- c("TP1" = "#fee090", "TP2" = "#fc8d59", "TP3" = "#d73027", "TP4" = "#4575b4")
```

---

# 1. Load Data

## 1a. Lipidomics

Load the processed lipid species data saved by `06-lipidomics-analysis.Rmd`. If the `.rds`
file is not yet present (i.e., the upstream script has not been run), this chunk re-reads and
re-processes the raw data using the same filtering and normalization pipeline.

```{r load-lipids}
lipid_rds <- "M-multi-species/data/lipidomics/lipids.rds"

if (file.exists(lipid_rds)) {

  lipids <- readRDS(lipid_rds)

} else {

  # ── Batch 1 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  lq1 <- read_xlsx(
    "M-multi-species/data/lipidomics/2025-02-05_Roberts_Test_Coral.xlsx",
    sheet = "Species Quant"
  ) %>%
    rename(sample = `Sample ID`, number_measured = `# of Measured Lipid Species`)

  lq1[lq1 == "."] <- NA

  lq1_wide <- as.data.frame(lapply(names(lq1), function(col) {
    if (col == "sample") lq1[[col]] else as.numeric(as.character(lq1[[col]]))
  }))
  colnames(lq1_wide) <- names(lq1)

  lq1_long <- lq1_wide %>%
    select(!number_measured) %>%
    pivot_longer(names_to = "lipid", values_to = "nmol.g_plasma", cols = c(2:1361)) %>%
    mutate(
      species   = case_when(sample == "L26" ~ "Acropora",
                            sample == "L39" ~ "Porites",
                            sample == "L67" ~ "Acropora",
                            sample == "L80" ~ "Porites",
                            sample == "L84" ~ "Pocillopora"),
      timepoint = case_when(sample == "L26" ~ "TP4", sample == "L39" ~ "TP2",
                            sample == "L67" ~ "TP1", sample == "L80" ~ "TP2",
                            sample == "L84" ~ "TP3"),
      colony    = case_when(sample == "L26" ~ "ACR-229", sample == "L39" ~ "POR-216",
                            sample == "L67" ~ "ACR-150", sample == "L80" ~ "POR-83",
                            sample == "L84" ~ "POC-52"),
      type      = case_when(sample == "prepared_blank_01" ~ "blank",
                            sample %in% c("QC_01","QC_02") ~ "QC",
                            TRUE ~ "sample"),
      protein.ug = case_when(sample == "L26" ~ 340.2, sample == "L39" ~ 139.2,
                             sample == "L67" ~ 7.3,   sample == "L80" ~ 35.0,
                             sample == "L84" ~ 185.9)
    )

  lq1_long <- lq1_long %>% filter(!type %in% c("QC"))

  blanks1 <- lq1_long %>% filter(type == "blank") %>%
    group_by(lipid) %>% summarise(mean_blank = mean(nmol.g_plasma, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace_na(., 0)))

  lq1_long <- lq1_long %>%
    filter(!type == "blank") %>%
    left_join(blanks1) %>%
    mutate(nmol.g_plasma.corr = pmax(nmol.g_plasma - mean_blank, 0)) %>%
    group_by(lipid) %>%
    filter(!any(type == "sample" & is.na(nmol.g_plasma.corr))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein = (nmol.g_plasma.corr * 25) / protein.ug) %>%
    select(sample, lipid, colony, timepoint, species, type, nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein)

  # ── Batch 2 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  lq2 <- read_xlsx(
    "M-multi-species/data/lipidomics/2025-02-20_Roberts_QuantLipidData.xlsx",
    sheet = "Species Quant"
  ) %>%
    rename(sample = `Sample ID`, number_measured = `# of Measured Lipids`,
           tube = `Serial Number`, batch = Batch, protein.ug = `Protein Count, µg`)

  lq2[lq2 == "."] <- NA

  lq2_wide <- as.data.frame(lapply(names(lq2), function(col) {
    if (col == "sample") lq2[[col]] else as.numeric(as.character(lq2[[col]]))
  }))
  colnames(lq2_wide) <- names(lq2)

  lq2_long <- lq2_wide %>%
    select(!number_measured) %>%
    pivot_longer(names_to = "lipid", values_to = "nmol.g_plasma",
                 cols = -c(sample, batch, tube, protein.ug)) %>%
    mutate(
      colony    = str_extract(sample, "^[^_]+"),
      timepoint = str_extract(sample, "(?<=_).*"),
      species   = case_when(str_detect(sample, "ACR") ~ "Acropora",
                            str_detect(sample, "POC") ~ "Pocillopora",
                            str_detect(sample, "POR") ~ "Porites",
                            TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      type      = case_when(str_detect(sample, "blank") ~ "blank",
                            str_detect(sample, "QC_")   ~ "QC",
                            str_detect(sample, "PBQC")  ~ "PBQC",
                            TRUE ~ "sample")
    )

  lq2_long <- lq2_long %>% filter(!type == "QC")

  blanks2 <- lq2_long %>% filter(type == "blank") %>%
    group_by(lipid, batch) %>% summarise(mean_blank = mean(nmol.g_plasma, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace_na(., 0)))

  lq2_long <- lq2_long %>%
    filter(!type == "blank") %>%
    left_join(blanks2) %>%
    mutate(nmol.g_plasma.corr = pmax(nmol.g_plasma - mean_blank, 0)) %>%
    group_by(lipid) %>%
    filter(!any(type == "sample" & is.na(nmol.g_plasma.corr))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein = (nmol.g_plasma.corr * 25) / protein.ug) %>%
    select(sample, lipid, colony, timepoint, species, type, nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein)

  # ── Combine & final filter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  lipids_all <- rbind(lq1_long, lq2_long)

  na_cols <- lipids_all %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = lipid, values_from = nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything()) %>% filter(value > 0) %>% pull(name)

  lipids <- lipids_all %>%
    filter(!lipid %in% na_cols) %>%
    filter(!type == "PBQC")

  saveRDS(lipids, lipid_rds)
}

cat("Lipid data: ", nrow(lipids), "rows,",
    length(unique(lipids$lipid)), "lipids,",
    length(unique(lipids$colony)), "colonies\n")
```

## 1b. Metabolomics

Load the processed metabolite data saved by `07-metabolomics-analysis.Rmd`. If the `.rds`
file is not yet present this chunk re-reads and re-processes the raw data.

```{r load-metabolites}
metab_rds <- "M-multi-species/data/metabolomics/metabolites.rds"

standards <- c(
  "3C13-Glycine","4C13-Alanine","2C13-Choline","4C13-Serine","d3-Creatinine",
  "6C13-Proline","6C13-Valine","5C13-Threonine","5C13-Aspartic Acid","6C13-Asparagine",
  "7C13-Leucine","7C13-iso-Leucine","2C13-Glutamic acid","7C13-Glutamine",
  "6C13-Glutamic acid","8C13-Lysine","6C13-Methionine","9C13-Histidine",
  "10C13-Phenylalanine","2C13-Tyrosine","10C13-Arginine","10C13-Tyrosine",
  "13C13-Tryptophan","8C13-Cystine","11C13-Uridine","3C13-Lactate","4C13-3HBA",
  "2N15-Xanthine","2N15-Urate","1C13-Citrulline","6C13-Glucose","4C13-Pentothenate"
)

if (file.exists(metab_rds)) {

  metabs <- readRDS(metab_rds)

} else {

  mq <- read_xlsx("M-multi-species/data/metabolomics/2025-04-15_Roberts-98.xlsx",
                  sheet = "Relative Quant Data") %>%
    rename(compound = `Current MS Compounds`)

  mq[mq == "N/A"] <- NA
  mq <- mq %>% select(!any_of(c("HMDB ID", "KEGG ID")))

  mq_wide <- as.data.frame(lapply(names(mq), function(col) {
    if (col == "compound") mq[[col]] else as.numeric(as.character(mq[[col]]))
  }))
  colnames(mq_wide) <- names(mq)

  mq_long <- mq_wide %>%
    pivot_longer(names_to = "sample", values_to = "rel.quant", cols = -compound) %>%
    mutate(
      colony    = str_extract(sample, "^[^_]+"),
      timepoint = str_extract(sample, "(?<=_).*"),
      species   = case_when(str_detect(sample, "ACR") ~ "Acropora",
                            str_detect(sample, "POC") ~ "Pocillopora",
                            str_detect(sample, "POR") ~ "Porites",
                            TRUE ~ NA_character_),
      type      = if_else(str_detect(sample, "PBQC"), "PBQC", "sample")
    )

  sites <- read_csv("M-multi-species/data/phys_master_timeseries.csv") %>%
    select(colony_id_corr, site) %>% rename(colony = colony_id_corr)
  mq_long <- left_join(mq_long, sites) %>% unique()

  protein <- read_xlsx("M-multi-species/data/metabolomics/2025-04-15_Roberts-98.xlsx",
                       sheet = "Protein")
  mq_long <- left_join(mq_long, protein)

  # Remove standards
  mq_long <- mq_long %>% filter(!compound %in% standards)

  # Keep only compounds detected in at least one PBQC
  not_in_pbqc <- mq_long %>%
    group_by(compound) %>%
    filter(type == "PBQC" & is.na(rel.quant)) %>%
    pull(compound) %>% unique()
  mq_long <- mq_long %>% filter(!compound %in% not_in_pbqc)

  # Remove compounds with >10% NA across samples
  keep_compounds <- mq_long %>%
    group_by(compound) %>%
    summarise(na_prop = sum(is.na(rel.quant)) / n()) %>%
    filter(na_prop < 0.1) %>% pull(compound)
  mq_long <- mq_long %>% filter(compound %in% keep_compounds)

  # Remove PBQCs and normalize
  mq_long <- mq_long %>%
    filter(type != "PBQC") %>%
    select(!type) %>%
    mutate(rel.quant.ug = rel.quant / protein.ug) %>%
    select(!c(protein.ug, rel.quant))

  # Impute with group median
  metabs <- mq_long %>%
    group_by(compound, species, timepoint, site) %>%
    mutate(rel.quant.ug = if_else(is.na(rel.quant.ug),
                                  median(rel.quant.ug, na.rm = TRUE),
                                  rel.quant.ug)) %>%
    ungroup()

  saveRDS(metabs, metab_rds)
}

cat("Metabolite data:", nrow(metabs), "rows,",
    length(unique(metabs$compound)), "compounds,",
    length(unique(metabs$colony)), "colonies\n")
```

## 1c. Merge datasets

Match on `colony` + `timepoint`. Both datasets use the same colonies from the same
biological samples at each time point.

```{r merge}
# ── Lipids: mean per colony × timepoint (some colonies appear in both batches)
lipids_summary <- lipids %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  group_by(colony, species, timepoint, lipid) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(data_type = "lipid", feature = lipid) %>%
  select(colony, species, timepoint, feature, value, data_type)

# ── Metabolites
metabs_summary <- metabs %>%
  group_by(colony, species, timepoint, compound) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(rel.quant.ug, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(data_type = "metabolite", feature = compound) %>%
  select(colony, species, timepoint, feature, value, data_type)

# ── Combined long-form (keep data_type for heatmaps/plots)
combined_long <- bind_rows(lipids_summary, metabs_summary)

# ── Identify colonies with BOTH lipid and metabolite data
colonies_both <- intersect(
  unique(lipids_summary$colony),
  unique(metabs_summary$colony)
)
cat("Colonies with both datasets:", length(colonies_both), "\n")

combined_long <- combined_long %>%
  filter(colony %in% colonies_both)

# ── Wide matrix: rows = colony×timepoint, cols = all features
# Pivot each dataset separately then join — avoids the data_type column
# causing pivot_wider to keep lipid and metabolite rows on separate lines.
lip_wide_tmp <- lipids_summary %>%
  filter(colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
  select(-data_type) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = value)

met_wide_tmp <- metabs_summary %>%
  filter(colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
  select(-data_type) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = value)

combined_wide <- inner_join(lip_wide_tmp, met_wide_tmp,
                            by = c("colony", "species", "timepoint")) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

cat("Integrated matrix:", nrow(combined_wide), "samples ×",
    ncol(combined_wide) - 3, "features\n")

# ── Keep ordered timepoint factor
tp_order <- c("TP1","TP2","TP3","TP4")
combined_wide <- combined_wide %>%
  mutate(timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = tp_order))
```

# 2. Species and Timepoint Effects on Combined Profile

## 2a. PERMANOVA – combined lipid + metabolite matrix

```{r permanova-combined}
meta_cols  <- c("colony", "species", "timepoint")
feat_mat   <- combined_wide %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols))
meta_df    <- combined_wide %>% select(all_of(meta_cols))

feat_scaled <- scale(feat_mat)

set.seed(42)
perm_combined <- adonis2(feat_scaled ~ species * timepoint,
                         data = meta_df, method = "eu", permutations = 999)
print(perm_combined)
```

adonis2(formula = feat_scaled ~ species * timepoint, data = meta_df, permutations = 999, method = "eu")
                  Df SumOfSqs      R2       F Pr(>F)    
species            2    14994 0.30826 22.2191  0.001 ***
timepoint          3     2135 0.04390  2.1093  0.012 *  
species:timepoint  4     2494 0.05127  1.8478  0.016 *  
Residual          86    29017 0.59657                   
Total             95    48640 1.00000  

## 2b. PCA – joint visualisation

```{r pca-combined, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
pca_combined <- prcomp(feat_scaled, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)

pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca_combined$x[, 1:4]) %>%
  bind_cols(meta_df)

var_exp <- round(summary(pca_combined)$importance[2, 1:4] * 100, 1)

p_species <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = species, shape = timepoint)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = species), level = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = species_cols) +
  labs(title = "Combined lipid + metabolite PCA",
       subtitle = "Coloured by species",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", var_exp[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", var_exp[2], "%)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

p_time <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = timepoint, shape = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = timepoint), level = 0.75, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = timepoint_cols) +
  labs(title = "Combined lipid + metabolite PCA",
       subtitle = "Coloured by timepoint",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", var_exp[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", var_exp[2], "%)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

p_species + p_time
```

## 2c. Within-species PERMANOVA – timepoint effect

```{r permanova-within-species}
species_list <- c("Acropora", "Pocillopora", "Porites")

within_sp_results <- lapply(species_list, function(sp) {
  sub_wide  <- combined_wide %>% filter(species == sp)
  sub_feat  <- scale(sub_wide %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols)))
  sub_meta  <- sub_wide %>% select(all_of(meta_cols))
  res <- adonis2(sub_feat ~ timepoint, data = sub_meta,
                 method = "eu", permutations = 999)
  data.frame(species = sp,
             R2      = round(res$R2[1], 3),
             F       = round(res$F[1], 2),
             p       = res$`Pr(>F)`[1])
})

within_sp_df <- bind_rows(within_sp_results)
print(within_sp_df)
```

      species    R2    F     p
1    Acropora 0.081 1.15 0.292
2 Pocillopora 0.167 2.60 0.026
3     Porites 0.105 1.32 0.207

# 3. Multi-block Integration with DIABLO (mixOmics)

DIABLO identifies latent components that maximally co-vary across the two omics blocks
while discriminating groups (here: species). This reveals molecules whose joint variation
distinguishes species and time.

## 3a. Prepare blocks

```{r diablo-prep}
# Subset to colonies that have both data types
lip_wide_blk <- lipids %>%
  filter(type == "sample", colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
  group_by(colony, species, timepoint, lipid) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = lipid, values_from = value) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

met_wide_blk <- metabs %>%
  filter(colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
  group_by(colony, species, timepoint, compound) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(rel.quant.ug, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = compound, values_from = value) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

# Align on the same colony × timepoint
key_lip <- paste(lip_wide_blk$colony, lip_wide_blk$timepoint)
key_met <- paste(met_wide_blk$colony, met_wide_blk$timepoint)
common_keys <- intersect(key_lip, key_met)

lip_blk <- lip_wide_blk %>%
  filter(paste(colony, timepoint) %in% common_keys) %>%
  arrange(colony, timepoint)

met_blk <- met_wide_blk %>%
  filter(paste(colony, timepoint) %in% common_keys) %>%
  arrange(colony, timepoint)

# Matrices
X_lip <- as.matrix(lip_blk %>% select(where(is.numeric)))
X_met <- as.matrix(met_blk %>% select(where(is.numeric)))

# Outcome: species (for supervised DIABLO)
Y_sp  <- factor(lip_blk$species)
meta_blk <- lip_blk %>% select(colony, species, timepoint)

cat("DIABLO blocks: lipids", nrow(X_lip), "×", ncol(X_lip),
    "| metabolites", nrow(X_met), "×", ncol(X_met), "\n")
```

## 3b. Run DIABLO (species discrimination)

```{r diablo-species, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
set.seed(42)

# Initial run to get design
design_mat <- matrix(0.1, nrow = 2, ncol = 2,
                     dimnames = list(c("lipid","metabolite"),
                                     c("lipid","metabolite")))
diag(design_mat) <- 0

diablo_res <- block.splsda(
  X    = list(lipid = X_lip, metabolite = X_met),
  Y    = Y_sp,
  ncomp = 2,
  keepX = list(lipid = c(20, 20), metabolite = c(20, 20)),
  design = design_mat
)

# Individual sample plots per block
plotIndiv(diablo_res,
          ind.names = FALSE,
          legend = TRUE,
          title  = "DIABLO – species discrimination",
          ellipse = TRUE,
          col.per.group = unname(species_cols[levels(Y_sp)]))
```

## 3c. DIABLO – arrow plot showing co-inertia between blocks

```{r diablo-arrow, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
plotArrow(diablo_res,
          ind.names = FALSE,
          legend     = TRUE,
          title      = "DIABLO arrow plot: lipid → metabolite")
```

## 3d. DIABLO – top loading variables per block

```{r diablo-loadings, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
plotLoadings(diablo_res,
             comp   = 1,
             contrib = "max",
             method  = "mean",
             title   = "DIABLO Comp 1 loadings")
```

## 3e. Circos plot – cross-block correlations

Displays the strongest positive and negative correlations between top lipids and top
metabolites on DIABLO component 1.

```{r circos, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
circosPlot(diablo_res,
           cutoff   = 0.6,
           line     = TRUE,
           color.blocks = c("#1b7837","#4575b4"),
           comp     = 1,
           size.labels = 1,
           size.variables = 0.7)
```

# 4. Heatmaps – Joint Z-score Profiles

## 4a. Combined z-score heatmap by species

Shows whether the same molecules are elevated or depleted in each species across both
data modalities simultaneously.

```{r heatmap-species, fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
# Select top variable features (variance across all samples)
n_top <- 50

top_features <- combined_long %>%
  group_by(feature, data_type) %>%
  summarise(feat_var = var(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(data_type) %>%
  slice_max(feat_var, n = n_top) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  pull(feature)

heat_sp <- combined_long %>%
  filter(feature %in% top_features) %>%
  group_by(feature) %>%
  mutate(z = as.numeric(scale(value))) %>%
  group_by(species, feature, data_type) %>%
  summarise(z_mean = mean(z, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = species, values_from = z_mean)

heat_mat_sp <- as.matrix(heat_sp %>% select(-feature, -data_type))
rownames(heat_mat_sp) <- heat_sp$feature

# Annotation: data type (lipid vs metabolite)
row_ann <- rowAnnotation(
  `Data type` = heat_sp$data_type,
  col = list(`Data type` = c(lipid = "#2166ac", metabolite = "#b2182b")),
  show_annotation_name = TRUE
)

Heatmap(
  heat_mat_sp,
  name           = "Z-score",
  col            = colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("#4575b4","white","#d73027")),
  left_annotation = row_ann,
  cluster_rows   = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  show_row_names  = FALSE,
  row_split       = heat_sp$data_type,
  row_title       = c("Lipid","Metabolite"),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  row_gap         = unit(3, "mm"),
  border          = TRUE,
  column_title    = "Top variable features (z-score) by species"
)
```

## 4b. Combined z-score heatmap by timepoint within each species

```{r heatmap-timepoint, fig.width=14, fig.height=12}
plot_tp_heatmap <- function(sp) {

  heat_tp <- combined_long %>%
    filter(feature %in% top_features, species == sp) %>%
    group_by(feature) %>%
    mutate(z = as.numeric(scale(value))) %>%
    group_by(timepoint, feature, data_type) %>%
    summarise(z_mean = mean(z, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = z_mean)

  # Reorder columns to timepoint order
  tp_cols_present <- tp_order[tp_order %in% names(heat_tp)]
  heat_tp <- heat_tp %>% select(feature, data_type, all_of(tp_cols_present))

  heat_mat_tp <- as.matrix(heat_tp %>% select(-feature, -data_type))
  rownames(heat_mat_tp) <- heat_tp$feature

  row_ann <- rowAnnotation(
    `Data type` = heat_tp$data_type,
    col = list(`Data type` = c(lipid = "#2166ac", metabolite = "#b2182b")),
    show_legend = FALSE
  )

  Heatmap(
    heat_mat_tp,
    name            = "Z-score",
    col             = colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("#4575b4","white","#d73027")),
    left_annotation = row_ann,
    cluster_rows    = TRUE,
    cluster_columns = FALSE,
    show_row_names  = FALSE,
    row_split       = heat_tp$data_type,
    row_title       = c("Lipid","Metabolite"),
    column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
    row_gap         = unit(3, "mm"),
    border          = TRUE,
    column_title    = paste(sp, "– top features by timepoint")
  )
}

draw(plot_tp_heatmap("Acropora"))
draw(plot_tp_heatmap("Pocillopora"))
draw(plot_tp_heatmap("Porites"))
```

# 5. Pairwise Correlation Between Lipids and Metabolites

## 5a. Compute correlations (Spearman) within each species

For each species, correlate the colony-level mean of every lipid against every metabolite
across timepoints. Correlations use **colony-level means** (n = number of colonies ×
timepoints with both datasets), giving a single correlation per lipid–metabolite pair
per species.

```{r compute-correlations}
compute_correlations <- function(sp) {

  lip_sp <- lipids %>%
    filter(type == "sample", species == sp, colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
    group_by(colony, timepoint, lipid) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  met_sp <- metabs %>%
    filter(species == sp, colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
    group_by(colony, timepoint, compound) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(rel.quant.ug, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  # Pivot wide and align
  lip_w <- lip_sp %>% pivot_wider(names_from = lipid, values_from = value)
  met_w <- met_sp %>% pivot_wider(names_from = compound, values_from = value)

  key_l <- paste(lip_w$colony, lip_w$timepoint)
  key_m <- paste(met_w$colony, met_w$timepoint)
  shared <- intersect(key_l, key_m)

  lip_w <- lip_w %>% filter(paste(colony, timepoint) %in% shared) %>%
    arrange(colony, timepoint)
  met_w <- met_w %>% filter(paste(colony, timepoint) %in% shared) %>%
    arrange(colony, timepoint)

  L <- as.matrix(lip_w %>% select(where(is.numeric)))
  M <- as.matrix(met_w %>% select(where(is.numeric)))

  # Pairwise Spearman correlations
  cor_mat  <- cor(L, M, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

  # p-values via permutation for large matrices can be slow; use psych::corr.test
  # approach (approximation)
  n        <- nrow(L)
  t_stat   <- cor_mat * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - cor_mat^2))
  p_mat    <- 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = n - 2, lower.tail = FALSE)

  # Reshape
  cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) %>%
    rename(lipid = Var1, compound = Var2, rho = Freq)
  p_long   <- as.data.frame(as.table(p_mat)) %>%
    rename(lipid = Var1, compound = Var2, p_val = Freq)

  left_join(cor_long, p_long, by = c("lipid","compound")) %>%
    mutate(species = sp,
           p_adj   = p.adjust(p_val, method = "BH"),
           sig      = p_adj < 0.05)
}

cor_list <- lapply(species_list, compute_correlations)
names(cor_list) <- species_list

# Count significant pairs
lapply(cor_list, function(d) sum(d$sig, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## 5b. Correlation heatmap – top significant pairs per species

```{r cor-heatmap, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
plot_cor_heatmap <- function(sp, n_top_lip = 25, n_top_met = 25) {

  df <- cor_list[[sp]] %>% filter(!is.na(rho))

  # Pick top lipids and metabolites with most significant correlations
  top_lip <- df %>% filter(sig) %>%
    count(lipid, sort = TRUE) %>% head(n_top_lip) %>% pull(lipid)
  top_met <- df %>% filter(sig) %>%
    count(compound, sort = TRUE) %>% head(n_top_met) %>% pull(compound)

  if (length(top_lip) == 0 | length(top_met) == 0) {
    # Fallback: use top by absolute rho
    top_lip <- df %>% group_by(lipid) %>%
      summarise(max_rho = max(abs(rho), na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
      slice_max(max_rho, n = n_top_lip) %>% pull(lipid)
    top_met <- df %>% group_by(compound) %>%
      summarise(max_rho = max(abs(rho), na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
      slice_max(max_rho, n = n_top_met) %>% pull(compound)
  }

  mat <- df %>%
    filter(lipid %in% top_lip, compound %in% top_met) %>%
    select(lipid, compound, rho) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = compound, values_from = rho) %>%
    column_to_rownames("lipid") %>%
    as.matrix()

  # Significance overlay — keep as logical matrix
  sig_mat <- df %>%
    filter(lipid %in% top_lip, compound %in% top_met) %>%
    select(lipid, compound, sig) %>%
    mutate(sig = as.integer(sig)) %>%          # integer avoids mixed-type coercion
    pivot_wider(names_from = compound, values_from = sig) %>%
    column_to_rownames("lipid") %>%
    as.matrix()

  # Align sig_mat rows/cols to match mat (clustering may reorder later, but
  # cell_fun uses pre-clustering indices so this ensures lookup is correct)
  mat     <- mat[rownames(mat), colnames(mat), drop = FALSE]
  sig_mat <- sig_mat[rownames(mat), colnames(mat), drop = FALSE]

  Heatmap(
    mat,
    name            = "Spearman ρ",
    col             = colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1), c("#4575b4","white","#d73027")),
    cluster_rows    = TRUE,
    cluster_columns = TRUE,
    show_row_names  = TRUE,
    show_column_names = TRUE,
    row_names_gp    = gpar(fontsize = 7),
    column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7),
    row_names_max_width = unit(6, "cm"),
    column_names_max_height = unit(6, "cm"),
    border          = TRUE,
    cell_fun = function(j, i, x, y, width, height, fill) {
      if (!is.na(sig_mat[i, j]) && sig_mat[i, j] == 1L) {
        grid.text("*", x, y, gp = gpar(fontsize = 8, col = "black"))
      }
    },
    column_title = paste(sp, "– lipid × metabolite Spearman ρ (* FDR<0.05)")
  )
}

draw(plot_cor_heatmap("Acropora"))
draw(plot_cor_heatmap("Pocillopora"))
draw(plot_cor_heatmap("Porites"))
```

# 6. Lag Correlation Analysis

Lag-correlation tests whether a change in one molecule at time **t** predicts a change
in another molecule at time **t+1** (or t−1). This reveals potential regulatory or
metabolic sequences — e.g., lipid catabolism at TP1 driving metabolite changes at TP3.

Timepoints are treated as ordered: TP1 < TP2 < TP3 < TP4. For species without TP2
(Acropora, Pocillopora), the sequence is TP1→TP3→TP4 (3 ordered steps).

## 6a. Compute cross-correlation at lag 0 and lag 1

```{r lag-cor}
compute_lag_cors <- function(sp, top_n = 30) {

  # Colony-mean per timepoint
  lip_sp <- lipids %>%
    filter(type == "sample", species == sp, colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
    group_by(colony, timepoint, lipid) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  met_sp <- metabs %>%
    filter(species == sp, colony %in% colonies_both) %>%
    group_by(colony, timepoint, compound) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(rel.quant.ug, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  # Ordered timepoint sequence for this species
  tps <- if (sp == "Porites") c("TP1","TP2","TP3","TP4") else c("TP1","TP3","TP4")
  tps <- tps[tps %in% unique(lip_sp$timepoint)]

  if (length(tps) < 3) {
    message(sp, ": insufficient timepoints for lag correlation")
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Average across colonies at each timepoint → one value per feature × timepoint
  lip_avg <- lip_sp %>%
    group_by(timepoint, lipid) %>%
    summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(timepoint %in% tps)

  met_avg <- met_sp %>%
    group_by(timepoint, compound) %>%
    summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(timepoint %in% tps)

  # Select top variable features to keep computation tractable
  top_lip_var <- lip_avg %>%
    group_by(lipid) %>% summarise(v = var(mean_val, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
    slice_max(v, n = top_n) %>% pull(lipid)

  top_met_var <- met_avg %>%
    group_by(compound) %>% summarise(v = var(mean_val, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
    slice_max(v, n = top_n) %>% pull(compound)

  lip_avg <- lip_avg %>% filter(lipid %in% top_lip_var)
  met_avg <- met_avg %>% filter(compound %in% top_met_var)

  # Pivot to timepoint × feature matrices (ordered)
  L_mat <- lip_avg %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = lipid,    values_from = mean_val) %>%
    arrange(match(timepoint, tps)) %>%
    select(-timepoint) %>%
    as.matrix()

  M_mat <- met_avg %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = compound, values_from = mean_val) %>%
    arrange(match(timepoint, tps)) %>%
    select(-timepoint) %>%
    as.matrix()

  n_tp <- nrow(L_mat)

  # Lag 0: contemporaneous (all timepoints)
  r0 <- cor(L_mat, M_mat, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

  # Lag +1: lipid at t predicts metabolite at t+1
  r_lag1_L_lead <- cor(L_mat[-n_tp, ], M_mat[-1, ],
                        method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

  # Lag -1: metabolite at t predicts lipid at t+1
  r_lag1_M_lead <- cor(M_mat[-n_tp, ], L_mat[-1, ],
                        method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

  # Long format
  to_long <- function(mat, lag_label, lip_col, met_col) {
    as.data.frame(as.table(mat)) %>%
      rename(!!lip_col := Var1, !!met_col := Var2, rho = Freq) %>%
      mutate(lag = lag_label, species = sp)
  }

  r0_long    <- to_long(r0, "lag_0",         "lipid", "compound")
  rp1_long   <- to_long(r_lag1_L_lead, "lag_+1 (lipid leads)", "lipid", "compound")
  rm1_long   <- to_long(r_lag1_M_lead, "lag_-1 (metab leads)", "compound", "lipid") %>%
    rename(lipid = compound, compound = lipid)

  bind_rows(r0_long, rp1_long, rm1_long)
}

lag_list  <- lapply(species_list, compute_lag_cors, top_n = 40)
names(lag_list) <- species_list
lag_all   <- bind_rows(lag_list)
```

Each panel is one species. Rows = lipid, columns = metabolite. Dot size = |ρ|,
dot colour = sign and lag direction. Only |ρ| ≥ 0.7 shown for clarity.

## 6d. Lag correlation timeline plot

For the most strongly lag-correlated pairs, plot both molecules across timepoints side
by side to visualise the offset.


```{r lag-timeline, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# Select one strong pair per species × lag for illustration
top_pairs <- lag_all %>%
  filter(abs(rho) >= 0.75, lag != "lag_0") %>%
  group_by(species, lag) %>%
  slice_max(abs(rho), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
 
plot_pair_timeline <- function(sp, lip_id, met_id, lag_label, rho_val) {
 
  tps <- if (sp == "Porites") c("TP1","TP2","TP3","TP4") else c("TP1","TP3","TP4")
 
  lip_ts <- lipids %>%
    filter(type == "sample", species == sp, lipid == lip_id) %>%
    group_by(timepoint) %>%
    summarise(mean = mean(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE),
              se   = sd(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(timepoint %in% tps) %>%
    mutate(feature = lip_id, data_type = "Lipid (nmol/µg protein)",
           tp_num = match(timepoint, tps))
 
  met_ts <- metabs %>%
    filter(species == sp, compound == met_id) %>%
    group_by(timepoint) %>%
    summarise(mean = mean(rel.quant.ug, na.rm = TRUE),
              se   = sd(rel.quant.ug, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(timepoint %in% tps) %>%
    mutate(feature = met_id, data_type = "Metabolite (rel/µg protein)",
           tp_num = match(timepoint, tps))
 
  bind_rows(lip_ts, met_ts) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = tp_num, y = mean, colour = data_type, group = data_type)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se, fill = data_type),
                alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(tps), labels = tps) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Lipid (nmol/µg protein)"        = "#2166ac",
                                   "Metabolite (rel/µg protein)"    = "#b2182b"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Lipid (nmol/µg protein)"        = "#2166ac",
                                 "Metabolite (rel/µg protein)"    = "#b2182b"),
                      name = NULL) +
    facet_wrap(~ data_type, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
    labs(title  = paste0(sp, ": ", lag_label),
         subtitle = paste0(lip_id, " × ", met_id, "  (ρ = ", round(rho_val, 2), ")"),
         x = "Timepoint", y = "Mean ± SE") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
 
if (nrow(top_pairs) > 0) {
  timeline_plots <- pmap(
    list(top_pairs$species, top_pairs$lipid, top_pairs$compound,
         top_pairs$lag, top_pairs$rho),
    plot_pair_timeline
  )
  wrap_plots(timeline_plots, ncol = 2)
} else {
  message("No pairs above |ρ| = 0.75 at non-zero lag; lower the threshold to generate plots.")
}
```

# 7. Lipid Class × Metabolic Pathway Summary

Group lipids by class (extracted from naming convention, e.g. "TG", "FFA", "PC") and
metabolites by functional category, then compute mean pairwise correlation within and
between groups to identify which lipid classes co-vary most with which metabolite groups.

```{r class-pathway, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# Extract lipid class from lipid name (prefix before first space)
# str_detect with ignore_case catches name variants from different batches/tools.
# Categories ordered roughly by metabolic module for a coherent x-axis.
cor_annotated <- bind_rows(cor_list) %>%
  mutate(
    lipid_class = sub(" .*", "", lipid),

    metab_category = case_when(

      # ── Glycolysis / TCA / central carbon ───────────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "glucose|fructose|galactose|mannose|ribose|G1P|G6P|F1P|F6P|
         glycerol.3|DHAP|3-phosphoglycerate|phosphoenolpyruvate|PEP|
         pyruvate|lactate|acetyl.CoA|citrate|isocitrate|aconitate|
         alpha.keto|2.oxoglutarate|succinyl|succinate|fumarate|malate|
         oxaloacetate|phosphogluconate|sedoheptulose",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "Central carbon / TCA",

      # ── Fatty acid β-oxidation & acylcarnitines ──────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "carnitine|acyl.coa|malonyl|acetoacetate|beta.hydroxy|
         3.hydroxy|ketone|hydroxybutyrate",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "Fatty acid metabolism",

      # ── Amino acids — branched chain ─────────────────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "\\bvaline\\b|\\bleucine\\b|\\bisoleucine\\b|
         \\bBCAA\\b|keto.isovalerate|keto.isocaproate|keto.methylvalerate",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "AA — branched chain",

      # ── Amino acids — aromatic ───────────────────────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "phenylalanine|tyrosine|tryptophan|kynurenine|
         indole|anthranilate|phenylpyruvate|hydroxyphenyl",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "AA — aromatic",

      # ── Amino acids — glucogenic / structural ────────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "\\balanine\\b|\\bglycine\\b|\\bserine\\b|\\bthreonine\\b|
         \\bproline\\b|hydroxyproline|\\bmethionine\\b|\\bcysteine\\b|
         \\blysine\\b|\\bhistidine\\b|\\bornithine\\b|\\basparagine\\b",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "AA — glucogenic / other",

      # ── Nitrogen assimilation, urea cycle & purines ──────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "glutamine|glutamic|aspartic|aspartate|arginine|citrulline|
         urea|urate|xanthine|hypoxanthine|inosine|xanthosine|
         S.adenosyl|SAM|SAH|carbamoyl",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "N-assimilation / urea cycle",

      # ── Symbiont exchange & DMSP / sulfur ───────────────────────────────
      # DMSP is the dominant organic sulfur compound produced by Symbiodiniaceae;
      # mycosporine-like AAs (MAAs) are UV protectants co-produced with symbiont.
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "DMSP|dimethylsulfoniopropion|dimethylsulfonio|
         DMS(?!O)|acrylate|mycosporine|shinorine|palythine|porphyra|
         MAA|\\bectoine\\b|proline.betaine",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "Symbiont exchange / DMSP",

      # ── Antioxidants & redox ─────────────────────────────────────────────
      # Coral–symbiont photosynthesis generates ROS; redox buffering is key.
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "glutathione|\\bGSH\\b|\\bGSSG\\b|ascorbate|dehydroascorbate|
         tocopherol|thioredoxin|cystine|ergothioneine|
         superoxide|catalase",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "Antioxidants / redox",

      # ── Energy carriers & nucleotides ────────────────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "\\bATP\\b|\\bADP\\b|\\bAMP\\b|\\bGTP\\b|\\bGDP\\b|\\bGMP\\b|
         \\bUTP\\b|\\bUDP\\b|\\bCTP\\b|\\bCDP\\b|
         \\bNAD\\b|NADH|NADP|\\bFAD\\b|FADH|
         phosphocreatine|\\bcreatine\\b|creatinine|
         \\bCoA\\b(?!.*carnitine)",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "Energy carriers / nucleotides",

      # ── Osmolytes & membrane lipid head-groups ───────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "\\btaurine\\b|\\bbetaine\\b|\\bcholine\\b|phosphocholine|
         glycerophosphocholine|ethanolamine|\\binositol\\b|
         \\bcAMP\\b|\\bcGMP\\b",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "Osmolytes / membrane signaling",

      # ── Vitamins & enzyme cofactors ──────────────────────────────────────
      str_detect(compound, regex(
        "thiamine|riboflavin|pyridoxal|pyridoxamine|pyridoxine|
         folate|tetrahydrofolate|cobalamin|pantothenate|pantothenic|
         biotin|niacin|nicotinamide|lipoate|lipoic",
        ignore_case = TRUE, comments = TRUE)) ~ "Vitamins / cofactors",

      TRUE ~ "Other / unclassified"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rho))

# Counts per category so you can see what landed where
cat_counts <- cor_annotated %>%
  distinct(compound, metab_category) %>%
  count(metab_category, sort = TRUE)
knitr::kable(cat_counts, caption = "Metabolites per category (all species pooled)")

# Mean ρ per lipid class × metabolite category × species
class_summary <- cor_annotated %>%
  group_by(species, lipid_class, metab_category) %>%
  summarise(mean_rho = mean(rho, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_sig    = sum(sig, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups  = "drop")

# Ordered x-axis: biological modules flow from photosynthate → lipid storage → signaling
cat_order <- c(
  "Central carbon / TCA",
  "Fatty acid metabolism",
  "AA — branched chain",
  "AA — aromatic",
  "AA — glucogenic / other",
  "N-assimilation / urea cycle",
  "Symbiont exchange / DMSP",
  "Antioxidants / redox",
  "Energy carriers / nucleotides",
  "Osmolytes / membrane signaling",
  "Vitamins / cofactors",
  "Other / unclassified"
)

# Main lipid classes (adjust if your data has others)
lip_classes <- c("TG","DG","FFA","FA","PC","PE","LPC","LPE",
                 "CE","Cer","SM","PI","PG","HexCer")

class_plot_df <- class_summary %>%
  filter(lipid_class %in% lip_classes,
         metab_category %in% cat_order) %>%
  mutate(
    metab_category = factor(metab_category, levels = cat_order),
    lipid_class    = factor(lipid_class,    levels = rev(lip_classes))
  )

ggplot(class_plot_df, aes(x = metab_category, y = lipid_class, fill = mean_rho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n_sig > 0, paste0("*", n_sig), "")),
            size = 3, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#4575b4", mid = "white", high = "#d73027",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "Mean\nSpearman ρ",
                       limits = c(-1, 1), na.value = "grey92") +
  labs(title    = "Lipid class × metabolite pathway correlations",
       subtitle = "* = number of FDR < 0.05 pairs; x-axis ordered by metabolic module",
       x = NULL, y = "Lipid class") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        legend.position = "right",
        panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines"))
```

# 8. Temporal Predictability of Metabolic State

Does the combined lipid × metabolite profile at timepoint **T** predict the
profile at **T+1**? We test this with four complementary approaches:

1. **Within-colony self-similarity** — is a colony more similar to itself
   across a transition than to other colonies?
2. **Mantel test** — are pairwise distances among colonies at Tn correlated
   with pairwise distances at Tn+1?
3. **PC-score lagged regression** — do PCA axis scores at Tn predict scores
   at Tn+1 (linear regression, leave-one-out cross-validated R²)?
4. **Trajectory plots** — ordination arrows visualise each colony's path
   through multivariate metabolic space.

Consecutive timepoint pairs used:
* Porites: TP1→TP2, TP2→TP3, TP3→TP4
* Acropora / Pocillopora: TP1→TP3, TP3→TP4

```{r temporal-setup}
# Helper: return consecutive TP pairs for each species
get_tp_pairs <- function(sp) {
  if (sp == "Porites") {
    list(c("TP1","TP2"), c("TP2","TP3"), c("TP3","TP4"))
  } else {
    list(c("TP1","TP3"), c("TP3","TP4"))
  }
}

tp_order <- c("TP1","TP2","TP3","TP4")

# PCA on the full combined feature matrix (already scaled in earlier section)
feat_all    <- combined_wide %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols))
feat_scaled_all <- scale(feat_all)
pca_all     <- prcomp(feat_scaled_all, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
pct_var     <- round(summary(pca_all)$importance[2, 1:5] * 100, 1)

pca_scores <- combined_wide %>%
  select(all_of(meta_cols)) %>%
  bind_cols(as_tibble(pca_all$x[, 1:5])) %>%
  mutate(tp_num = match(timepoint, tp_order))
```

## 8a. Within-colony self-similarity vs cross-colony similarity

For each colony and each consecutive transition, compute:

* **Self ρ** — Spearman correlation between that colony's feature vector at Tn
  and its own feature vector at Tn+1.
* **Cross ρ** — mean Spearman correlation between that colony's vector at Tn
  and every *other* colony's vector at Tn+1 (null expectation).

If metabolic state is predictable, self ρ should exceed cross ρ.

```{r self-similarity, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
self_sim_list <- purrr::map_dfr(unique(combined_wide$species), function(sp) {
  pairs  <- get_tp_pairs(sp)
  df_sp  <- combined_wide %>% filter(species == sp)

  purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pair) {
    t1 <- df_sp %>% filter(timepoint == pair[1]) %>% arrange(colony)
    t2 <- df_sp %>% filter(timepoint == pair[2]) %>% arrange(colony)
    shared <- intersect(t1$colony, t2$colony)
    if (length(shared) < 3) return(NULL)

    t1 <- t1 %>% filter(colony %in% shared) %>% arrange(colony)
    t2 <- t2 %>% filter(colony %in% shared) %>% arrange(colony)

    feat1 <- as.matrix(t1 %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols)))
    feat2 <- as.matrix(t2 %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols)))
    rownames(feat1) <- t1$colony
    rownames(feat2) <- t2$colony

    purrr::map_dfr(shared, function(col) {
      self_r  <- cor(feat1[col, ], feat2[col, ], method = "spearman")
      others  <- setdiff(shared, col)
      cross_r <- if (length(others) > 0)
        mean(sapply(others, function(o) cor(feat1[col, ], feat2[o, ], method = "spearman")))
      else NA_real_
      tibble(species    = sp,
             transition = paste0(pair[1], "→", pair[2]),
             colony     = col,
             self_rho   = self_r,
             cross_rho  = cross_r,
             delta_rho  = self_r - cross_r)
    })
  })
})

# Summary table
self_sim_summary <- self_sim_list %>%
  group_by(species, transition) %>%
  summarise(median_self  = round(median(self_rho,  na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            median_cross = round(median(cross_rho, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            median_delta = round(median(delta_rho, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            n_colonies   = n(),
            .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(self_sim_summary,
             caption = "Median self vs cross-colony Spearman ρ per transition")

# Plot
p_self <- self_sim_list %>%
  pivot_longer(c(self_rho, cross_rho), names_to = "type", values_to = "rho") %>%
  mutate(type = recode(type,
    self_rho  = "Self (same colony)",
    cross_rho = "Cross (other colonies)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = transition, y = rho, fill = type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, outlier.size = 1.5, width = 0.55,
               position = position_dodge(0.65)) +
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Self (same colony)"       = "#2166ac",
               "Cross (other colonies)"   = "#ef8a62"),
    name = NULL) +
  labs(title    = "Temporal self-similarity of the metabolic state",
       subtitle = "Self ρ > Cross ρ → state at T predicts state at T+1",
       x = "Timepoint transition", y = "Spearman ρ (feature vectors)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top",
        strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_delta <- self_sim_list %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = transition, y = delta_rho, colour = species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.4,
               colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Acropora   = "#E69F00",
                                 Pocillopora = "#56B4E9",
                                 Porites    = "#009E73"),
                      guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Δρ = Self ρ − Cross ρ (predictability advantage per colony)",
       x = "Timepoint transition", y = "Δρ") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        strip.text  = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_self / p_delta + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1))
```

## 8b. Mantel test: preservation of pairwise distances across transitions

If metabolic organisation at T predicts T+1, the pairwise Euclidean distance
matrix among colonies should be correlated across the two timepoints
(Mantel statistic r ≈ 1 → perfect preservation; r ≈ 0 → no predictability).

```{r mantel-test}
mantel_results <- purrr::map_dfr(unique(combined_wide$species), function(sp) {
  pairs  <- get_tp_pairs(sp)
  df_sp  <- combined_wide %>% filter(species == sp)

  purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pair) {
    t1 <- df_sp %>% filter(timepoint == pair[1]) %>% arrange(colony)
    t2 <- df_sp %>% filter(timepoint == pair[2]) %>% arrange(colony)
    shared <- intersect(t1$colony, t2$colony)
    if (length(shared) < 4) return(NULL)

    t1 <- t1 %>% filter(colony %in% shared) %>% arrange(colony)
    t2 <- t2 %>% filter(colony %in% shared) %>% arrange(colony)

    d1 <- dist(scale(t1 %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols))))
    d2 <- dist(scale(t2 %>% select(-all_of(meta_cols))))

    m <- vegan::mantel(d1, d2, method = "spearman", permutations = 999)
    tibble(species    = sp,
           transition = paste0(pair[1], "→", pair[2]),
           n_colonies = length(shared),
           mantel_r   = round(m$statistic, 3),
           p_value    = m$signif)
  })
})

knitr::kable(mantel_results,
             caption = "Mantel test: correlation of pairwise distance matrices across transitions (999 permutations)")
```

```{r mantel-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
mantel_results %>%
  mutate(sig_label = case_when(p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
                               p_value < 0.01  ~ "**",
                               p_value < 0.05  ~ "*",
                               TRUE            ~ "ns"),
         transition = factor(transition)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = transition, y = mantel_r, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sig_label, y = mantel_r + 0.03), size = 5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Acropora    = "#E69F00",
                                Pocillopora = "#56B4E9",
                                Porites     = "#009E73"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(NA, 1.05)) +
  labs(title = "Mantel r: preservation of pairwise metabolic distances across transitions",
       subtitle = "Higher r = colony metabolic organisation is maintained; * p < 0.05",
       x = "Timepoint transition", y = "Mantel r (Spearman)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        strip.text  = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## 8c. PC-score lagged regression

Project samples into PCA space. For each transition, regress PC1 (and PC2)
scores at **Tn+1** on scores at **Tn** across colonies. A high R² means the
position in ordination space at the previous timepoint predicts position at
the next. Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV) gives an honest estimate
of predictive accuracy.

```{r pc-prediction, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
loocv_r2 <- function(x, y) {
  # Leave-one-out cross-validated R² for y ~ x (simple linear)
  n <- length(x)
  if (n < 4) return(NA_real_)
  preds <- sapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    m <- lm(y[-i] ~ x[-i])
    predict(m, newdata = data.frame(`x[-i]` = x[i]))  # manual predict
    coef(m)[1] + coef(m)[2] * x[i]
  })
  ss_res  <- sum((y - preds)^2)
  ss_tot  <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
  max(0, 1 - ss_res / ss_tot)   # clip at 0 (can be negative)
}

pc_pred <- purrr::map_dfr(unique(pca_scores$species), function(sp) {
  pairs  <- get_tp_pairs(sp)
  df_sp  <- pca_scores %>% filter(species == sp)

  purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(pair) {
    t1 <- df_sp %>% filter(timepoint == pair[1]) %>% arrange(colony)
    t2 <- df_sp %>% filter(timepoint == pair[2]) %>% arrange(colony)
    shared <- intersect(t1$colony, t2$colony)
    if (length(shared) < 4) return(NULL)
    t1 <- t1 %>% filter(colony %in% shared) %>% arrange(colony)
    t2 <- t2 %>% filter(colony %in% shared) %>% arrange(colony)

    purrr::map_dfr(paste0("PC", 1:3), function(pc) {
      x <- t1[[pc]];  y <- t2[[pc]]
      m_full  <- lm(y ~ x)
      r2_full <- summary(m_full)$r.squared
      pval    <- summary(m_full)$coefficients[2, 4]
      r2_loo  <- loocv_r2(x, y)
      tibble(species    = sp,
             transition = paste0(pair[1], "→", pair[2]),
             pc         = pc,
             r2_full    = round(r2_full, 3),
             r2_loo     = round(r2_loo,  3),
             p_value    = round(pval,     4),
             n          = length(shared))
    })
  })
})

knitr::kable(pc_pred,
             caption = "Lagged PC-score regression: R² (full) and LOO-CV R² for predicting PC scores at Tn+1 from Tn")

# Dot plot of LOO-CV R² by species × transition × PC
pc_pred %>%
  mutate(sig_label = ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "*", ""),
         transition = factor(transition)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = transition, y = r2_loo, colour = pc, group = pc)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sig_label, y = r2_loo + 0.04), size = 5, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(PC1 = "#1b7837", PC2 = "#762a83", PC3 = "#d6604d"),
                      name = "PC axis") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(NA, 1)) +
  labs(title    = "LOO-CV R²: PC scores at Tn → PC scores at Tn+1",
       subtitle = "* p < 0.05 (full-model F-test); positive R² = predictive",
       x = "Timepoint transition", y = "LOO-CV R²") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "right",
        strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## 8d. Colony trajectory plots in PCA space

Arrows connect each colony's consecutive timepoints in PC1 × PC2 space.
Parallel, same-direction arrows suggest species-level temporal coordination
(predictable state transitions); criss-crossing arrows suggest idiosyncratic
or stochastic dynamics.

```{r trajectory-plot, fig.width=14, fig.height=5}
# Build arrow data: start at Tn, end at Tn+1, per colony
pca_arrows <- pca_scores %>%
  arrange(colony, tp_num) %>%
  group_by(colony, species) %>%
  mutate(PC1_end = lead(PC1),
         PC2_end = lead(PC2),
         tp_end  = lead(timepoint)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(PC1_end)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Convex hulls per species × timepoint (optional context layer)
hull_data <- pca_scores %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint) %>%
  slice(chull(PC1, PC2)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot() +
  # Faint convex hulls per timepoint
  geom_polygon(data = hull_data,
               aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, group = timepoint, fill = timepoint),
               alpha = 0.07, colour = NA) +
  # Trajectory arrows per colony
  geom_segment(data = pca_arrows,
               aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, xend = PC1_end, yend = PC2_end),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.22, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               linewidth = 0.7, colour = "grey30", alpha = 0.7) +
  # Sample points coloured by timepoint
  geom_point(data = pca_scores,
             aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = timepoint, shape = timepoint),
             size = 3.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  # Colony labels (optional — comment out if crowded)
  # geom_text(data = pca_scores, aes(x=PC1, y=PC2, label=colony), size=2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(TP1 = "#2166ac", TP2 = "#74add1",
               TP3 = "#fdae61", TP4 = "#d73027"),
    name = "Timepoint") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(TP1 = "#2166ac", TP2 = "#74add1",
               TP3 = "#fdae61", TP4 = "#d73027"),
    guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(TP1 = 16, TP2 = 17, TP3 = 15, TP4 = 18),
                     name = "Timepoint") +
  labs(title    = "Colony trajectories through metabolic state space (PC1 × PC2)",
       subtitle = "Arrows: Tn → Tn+1 per colony; shading: convex hull per timepoint",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", pct_var[1], "% variance)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "% variance)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))
```

# 10. Lipidome Composition Over Time

This section examines how the **overall composition of the lipidome** shifts across timepoints
within each species, focusing on two complementary axes:

1. **Fatty acid saturation** — the balance of saturated (SFA), monounsaturated (MUFA), and
   polyunsaturated (PUFA) lipid species, which reflects membrane fluidity, thermal adaptation,
   and energy storage strategy.
2. **Symbiosis-associated lipid markers** — lipid classes and high-PUFA species
   enriched in Symbiodiniaceae membranes or linked to photosynthate carbon translocation,
   compared with host-specific storage and membrane lipids.

```{r lipidome-composition-setup}
# ── Parse fatty acid unsaturation from lipid species names ─────────────────
# Lipid names encode unsaturation as "carbons:double_bonds", e.g.:
#   "PC 36:4"     → 4 total double bonds
#   "TG(16:0/18:1/18:2)" → sum = 3 double bonds
#   "Cer d18:1/24:0"     → sum = 1 double bond
# Strategy: extract ALL "digits:digits" tokens, sum the right-hand side.

lipid_unsat <- lipids %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract lipid class: everything before the first space or opening parenthesis
    # e.g. "PC 36:4" → "PC", "TG(16:0/18:1/18:2)" → "TG", "Cer d18:1/24:0" → "Cer"
    lipid_class = sub("[ (].*", "", lipid),
    db_tokens   = str_extract_all(lipid, "\\d+:(\\d+)"),
    total_db    = map_dbl(db_tokens, function(x) {
      if (length(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)
      sum(as.numeric(str_extract(x, "(?<=:)\\d+")), na.rm = TRUE)
    }),
    sat_class = case_when(
      total_db == 0            ~ "SFA",
      total_db == 1            ~ "MUFA",
      total_db %in% 2:3        ~ "PUFA (2-3)",
      total_db >= 4            ~ "PUFA (4+)",
      TRUE                     ~ NA_character_
    ),
    sat_broad = case_when(
      total_db == 0  ~ "SFA",
      total_db == 1  ~ "MUFA",
      total_db >= 2  ~ "PUFA",
      TRUE           ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(total_db))

# Check how many species were parsed vs missed
cat("Lipid species with parsed unsaturation:",
    sum(!is.na(lipid_unsat$total_db)), "/",
    nrow(lipid_unsat), "\n")

# Show lipid class breakdown
lipid_unsat %>%
  count(lipid_class, sat_broad) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sat_broad, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(lipid_class) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Number of lipid species by class and saturation category")
```

## 10a. Unsaturation Index Over Time

The abundance-weighted mean number of double bonds per lipid species (Unsaturation Index, UI)
reflects the overall degree of fatty acid unsaturation in the lipidome. Higher UI = more PUFA-rich.

```{r unsat-index, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# ── Colony-level weighted unsaturation index ───────────────────────────────
ui_colony <- lipid_unsat %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, colony) %>%
  summarise(
    UI = weighted.mean(total_db, nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Species × timepoint summary
ui_summary <- ui_colony %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_UI = mean(UI, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_UI   = sd(UI, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p_ui <- ggplot(ui_summary,
               aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_UI,
                   color = species, group = species)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_UI - se_UI, ymax = mean_UI + se_UI),
                width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(data = ui_colony,
              aes(y = UI), width = 0.05, alpha = 0.3, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = species_cols) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint",
       y = "Weighted mean double bonds\n(Unsaturation Index)",
       title = "Lipidome unsaturation index across timepoints",
       color = "Species") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(p_ui)

# ── Kruskal-Wallis test: does UI differ across timepoints within each species?
cat("\n--- Kruskal-Wallis test: UI ~ timepoint within species ---\n")
ui_kw <- ui_colony %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    p_value  = kruskal.test(UI ~ timepoint)$p.value,
    statistic = kruskal.test(UI ~ timepoint)$statistic,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(sig = case_when(p_value < 0.001 ~ "***",
                         p_value < 0.01  ~ "**",
                         p_value < 0.05  ~ "*",
                         TRUE            ~ "ns"))

knitr::kable(ui_kw, digits = 4,
             caption = "Kruskal-Wallis test of unsaturation index across timepoints")
```

## 10b. SFA / MUFA / PUFA Proportions Over Time

```{r sat-proportions, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
# ── Colony-level SFA/MUFA/PUFA proportions ─────────────────────────────────
sat_colony <- lipid_unsat %>%
  filter(!is.na(sat_broad)) %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, colony, sat_broad) %>%
  summarise(total_nmol = sum(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, colony) %>%
  mutate(prop = total_nmol / sum(total_nmol)) %>%
  ungroup()

sat_summary <- sat_colony %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, sat_broad) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_prop   = sd(prop, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(sat_broad = factor(sat_broad, levels = c("SFA", "MUFA", "PUFA")))

sat_cols <- c("SFA" = "#d73027", "MUFA" = "#fee090", "PUFA" = "#4575b4")

p_sat <- ggplot(sat_summary,
                aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_prop,
                    color = sat_broad, group = sat_broad)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +

                    ymax = mean_prop + se_prop),
                width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.7) +

  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Proportion of lipidome (nmol)",
       title = "SFA / MUFA / PUFA proportions across timepoints") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_sat)

# ── Stacked bar version for a cleaner view of shifts ───────────────────────
p_sat_bar <- ggplot(sat_summary,
                    aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_prop,
                        fill = sat_broad)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  #geom_errorbar(
  #  data = sat_summary %>% filter(sat_broad == "PUFA"),
  #  aes(ymin = 1 - se_prop, ymax = 1),
  #  width = 0.15, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray40"
  #) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sat_cols, name = "Saturation") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Proportion of lipidome",
       title = "Lipidome saturation composition (stacked)") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_sat_bar)
```

## 10c. PUFA Degree Breakdown (High-PUFA Tracking)

Highly polyunsaturated fatty acids (≥4 double bonds) include EPA (20:5), DHA (22:6), and
arachidonic acid (20:4), which are enriched in Symbiodiniaceae membranes and are key
photosynthate-linked molecules. Tracking PUFA (4+) separately reveals symbiont-linked
flux patterns.

```{r pufa-breakdown, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
# ── Colony-level PUFA-class proportions ────────────────────────────────────
pufa_colony <- lipid_unsat %>%
  filter(!is.na(sat_class)) %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, colony, sat_class) %>%
  summarise(total_nmol = sum(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, colony) %>%
  mutate(prop = total_nmol / sum(total_nmol)) %>%
  ungroup()

pufa_summary <- pufa_colony %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, sat_class) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_prop   = sd(prop, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(sat_class = factor(sat_class,
                            levels = c("SFA","MUFA","PUFA (2-3)","PUFA (4+)")))

pufa_cols <- c("SFA"      = "#d73027",
               "MUFA"     = "#fee090",
               "PUFA (2-3)" = "#74add1",
               "PUFA (4+)"  = "#313695")

p_pufa <- ggplot(pufa_summary,
                 aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_prop,
                     fill = sat_class)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pufa_cols, name = "Saturation class") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint",
       y = "Proportion of lipidome",
       title = "PUFA breakdown: low-PUFA (2-3 DB) vs high-PUFA (≥4 DB) across timepoints") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_pufa)

# ── High-PUFA (4+) proportion over time, line plot ─────────────────────────
hpufa_summary <- pufa_colony %>%
  filter(sat_class == "PUFA (4+)") %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
            se_prop   = sd(prop, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
            .groups = "drop")

p_hpufa_line <- ggplot(hpufa_summary,
                        aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_prop,
                            color = species, group = species)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_prop - se_prop,
                    ymax = mean_prop + se_prop),
                width = 0.15) +
  scale_color_manual(values = species_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint",
       y = "Proportion high-PUFA (≥4 DB)",
       title = "High-PUFA (≥4 double bonds) lipid proportion over time",
       color = "Species") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

print(p_hpufa_line)
```

## 10d. Symbiosis-Associated vs Host Lipid Markers

Coral lipidomes contain lipids whose origin and function differ between the host and the
symbiont. Here we classify lipid classes into functional groups:

- **Symbiont-enriched**: plastid/algal membrane classes (DGDG, MGDG, SQDG, betaine lipids)
  and high-PUFA glycerolipids that symbiont photosynthesis drives
- **Host storage**: triglycerides (TG), diacylglycerols (DG), cholesterol esters (CE) —
  reflecting energy reserves accumulated from photosynthate
- **Host membrane / stress signalling**: phosphatidylcholines (PC/LPC), ceramides (Cer),
  sphingomyelins (SM) — involved in host membrane homeostasis and symbiosis regulation

```{r symbiosis-lipid-markers, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# ── Identify available lipid classes ───────────────────────────────────────
avail_classes <- sort(unique(lipid_unsat$lipid_class))
cat("Lipid classes in dataset:\n")
print(avail_classes)

# ── Define functional groups (use classes present in this dataset) ──────────
symbiont_classes  <- intersect(avail_classes,
  c("DGDG","MGDG","SQDG","BL","DGTS","HexCer","Hex2Cer",
    "PE","PE-O","PE-P"))                           # algal membrane-enriched

host_storage      <- intersect(avail_classes,
  c("TG","DG","CE","WE","TG-O"))                    # host energy storage

host_membrane_sig <- intersect(avail_classes,
  c("PC","LPC","SM","Cer","Cer-NDS","Cer-NS",
    "LPE","PS","PI","PG","PA",
    "PC-O","PC-P","LPC-O"))                          # host membrane / signalling

# Any class not placed above is flagged
unclassified <- setdiff(avail_classes,
                        c(symbiont_classes, host_storage, host_membrane_sig))
cat("\nFunctional classification:\n")
cat("  Symbiont-enriched:   ", paste(symbiont_classes, collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("  Host storage:        ", paste(host_storage, collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("  Host membrane/sig:   ", paste(host_membrane_sig, collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("  Unclassified:        ", paste(unclassified, collapse=", "), "\n")

# ── Assign functional group ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
lipid_func <- lipid_unsat %>%
  mutate(
    func_group = case_when(
      lipid_class %in% symbiont_classes  ~ "Symbiont-enriched",
      lipid_class %in% host_storage      ~ "Host storage",
      lipid_class %in% host_membrane_sig ~ "Host membrane / signalling",
      TRUE                               ~ "Other / unclassified"
    )
  )

# ── Colony-level proportions by functional group ────────────────────────────
func_colony <- lipid_func %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, colony, func_group) %>%
  summarise(total_nmol = sum(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, colony) %>%
  mutate(prop = total_nmol / sum(total_nmol)) %>%
  ungroup()

func_summary <- func_colony %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, func_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_prop = mean(prop, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_prop   = sd(prop, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(func_group = factor(func_group,
    levels = c("Symbiont-enriched",
               "Host storage",
               "Host membrane / signalling",
               "Other / unclassified")))

func_cols <- c(
  "Symbiont-enriched"          = "#35978f",
  "Host storage"               = "#bf812d",
  "Host membrane / signalling" = "#762a83",
  "Other / unclassified"       = "#bababa"
)

# Stacked bar: functional composition over time
p_func_bar <- ggplot(func_summary,
                     aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_prop, fill = func_group)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = func_cols, name = "Functional group") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Proportion of lipidome (nmol)",
       title = "Lipidome functional composition over time") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

print(p_func_bar)

# Line plot for each functional group
p_func_line <- ggplot(func_summary,
                      aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_prop,
                          color = species, group = species)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_prop - se_prop,
                    ymax = mean_prop + se_prop),
                width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = species_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Proportion of lipidome",
       color  = "Species",
       title  = "Functional lipid group proportions over time by species") +
  facet_wrap(~ func_group, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "right")

print(p_func_line)
```

## 10e. Per-Class Abundance Heatmap Over Time

Tracks the mean abundance of each lipid class (z-scored within class) across timepoints,
separately per species, to highlight which classes rise or fall over the timeseries.

```{r class-time-heatmap, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# ── Mean abundance per class × species × timepoint ─────────────────────────
class_tp <- lipids %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  mutate(lipid_class = sub("[ (].*", "", lipid)) %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, lipid_class, colony) %>%
  summarise(colony_total = sum(nmol.g_plasma.ug_protein, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(species, timepoint, lipid_class) %>%
  summarise(mean_abund = mean(colony_total, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# Z-score within each species × class combination
class_tp_z <- class_tp %>%
  group_by(species, lipid_class) %>%
  mutate(z = as.numeric(scale(mean_abund))) %>%
  ungroup()

# Order classes by functional group for readability
class_order_df <- tibble(
  lipid_class = avail_classes,
  func_group = case_when(
    lipid_class %in% symbiont_classes  ~ "1_Symbiont",
    lipid_class %in% host_storage      ~ "2_Storage",
    lipid_class %in% host_membrane_sig ~ "3_Membrane",
    TRUE                               ~ "4_Other"
  )
) %>% arrange(func_group, lipid_class)

class_tp_z <- class_tp_z %>%
  mutate(lipid_class = factor(lipid_class, levels = class_order_df$lipid_class))

p_class_heat <- ggplot(class_tp_z,
                        aes(x = timepoint, y = lipid_class, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#4575b4", mid = "white", high = "#d73027",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "Z-score\n(within class)") +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Lipid class",
       title = "Lipid class abundance over time (z-scored within class)") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "right")

print(p_class_heat)
```




# 11. Metabolic Integration Network

Visualise the lipid class × metabolite pathway correlation structure as a **bipartite network graph** — one panel per species. Nodes represent lipid classes (squares) or metabolite pathway categories (circles); edges connect pairs with at least one FDR < 0.05 correlation, coloured by mean Spearman ρ and sized by the number of significant pairs. This translates the heatmap in Section 7 into a format where network density and connectivity are immediately apparent.

```{r network-setup}
# Install igraph / ggraph if needed
if (!requireNamespace("igraph",  quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("igraph")
if (!requireNamespace("ggraph",  quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggraph")
if (!requireNamespace("tidygraph", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("tidygraph")
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(tidygraph)
```

```{r network-graph, fig.width=18, fig.height=7}
# ── Build edge table from cor_annotated ──────────────────────────────────────
# Use only pairs with ≥1 significant correlation
# Summarise per lipid_class × metab_category × species

network_edges <- cor_annotated %>%
  group_by(species, lipid_class, metab_category) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rho = mean(rho,       na.rm = TRUE),
    n_sig    = sum(sig,        na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_sig > 0,
         lipid_class    != "",
         metab_category != "Other / unclassified") %>%
  rename(from = lipid_class, to = metab_category)

# Lipid classes to include (same set as heatmap + any that have sig edges)
lip_classes_net <- unique(network_edges$from)
met_cats_net    <- unique(network_edges$to)

# Node metadata
nodes_lip <- tibble(
  name      = lip_classes_net,
  node_type = "Lipid class"
)
nodes_met <- tibble(
  name      = met_cats_net,
  node_type = "Metabolite pathway"
)
all_nodes <- bind_rows(nodes_lip, nodes_met)

# ── Plot function ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plot_network <- function(sp) {

  edges_sp <- network_edges %>% filter(species == sp)

  if (nrow(edges_sp) == 0) {
    return(
      ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5,
                 label = paste0(sp, "\n(no significant correlations)"),
                 size = 5, colour = "grey50") +
        theme_void() +
        labs(title = sp)
    )
  }

  # Keep only nodes that appear in this species' edges
  used_nodes <- all_nodes %>%
    filter(name %in% c(edges_sp$from, edges_sp$to))

  g <- tbl_graph(nodes = used_nodes, edges = edges_sp, directed = FALSE)

  # Edge colour scale: same diverging palette as heatmap
  ggraph(g, layout = "stress") +
    geom_edge_link(
      aes(edge_colour = mean_rho, edge_width = n_sig),
      alpha = 0.85
    ) +
    geom_node_point(
      aes(shape = node_type, colour = node_type),
      size = 7
    ) +
    geom_node_text(
      aes(label = name),
      repel = TRUE,
      size  = 3.2,
      max.overlaps = 30,
      colour = "grey15"
    ) +
    scale_edge_colour_gradient2(
      low      = "#4575b4",
      mid      = "grey90",
      high     = "#d73027",
      midpoint = 0,
      name     = "Mean ρ",
      limits   = c(-1, 1)
    ) +
    scale_edge_width_continuous(
      range = c(0.5, 4),
      name  = "# sig pairs"
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Lipid class" = 15, "Metabolite pathway" = 19),
      name   = NULL
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("Lipid class" = "#1a6137", "Metabolite pathway" = "#7b3294"),
      name   = NULL
    ) +
    labs(title = sp) +
    theme_graph(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5)
    )
}

p_net_acr <- plot_network("Acropora")
p_net_poc <- plot_network("Pocillopora")
p_net_por <- plot_network("Porites")

p_net_acr | p_net_poc | p_net_por
```

**Interpretation:** Network density directly reflects the degree of metabolic integration between lipid classes and metabolite pathways. Dense, richly connected networks (many edges, high edge width) indicate that lipid remodelling and metabolic flux co-vary tightly — the hallmark of a boom-and-bust physiological strategy where symbiont dynamics drive whole-system co-fluctuation. Sparse or empty networks indicate that each metabolic pool is independently regulated, consistent with a stable, homeostatic strategy.

---

# 12. Integrated Summary Figures (A–E)

This section assembles the five core figures that together tell the integrative story of species-specific lipid–metabolite co-regulation, temporal dynamics, and symbiosis strategy.

## Fig A — Lipid Class × Metabolite Pathway Heatmap

*Cross-species comparison of lipid class – metabolite pathway correlations. Tile intensity = mean Spearman ρ; asterisk + count = number of FDR < 0.05 pairs.*

```{r fig-A, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}

fig_A <- ggplot(class_plot_df,
                aes(x = metab_category, y = lipid_class, fill = mean_rho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n_sig > 0, paste0("*", n_sig), "")),
            size = 2.8, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#4575b4", mid = "white", high = "#d73027",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "Mean\nSpearman ρ",
                       limits = c(-1, 1), na.value = "grey92") +
  labs(title    = "Fig A — Lipid class × metabolite pathway correlations",
       subtitle = "* = number of FDR < 0.05 pairs; x-axis ordered by metabolic module",
       x = NULL, y = "Lipid class") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),

        panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines"))
fig_A
```

## Fig B — Metabolic Integration Network

```{r fig-B, fig.width=18, fig.height=7}
(p_net_acr | p_net_poc | p_net_por) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
```
